body:
Falls out of #199 landing after #205 was written.

#205 restores 11 of the 17 records demoted in error and holds 6 —
`CHEBI:756054` carbomycin, `759883` colistin sulfate, `759884` gentamicin,
`753395` lysostaphin, `748901` netilmicin, `759086` polymyxin B — because they
genuinely do not resolve in the local ChEBI build (max accession 747618, release
252) though they are real per OLS4. Both #205's manifest rows and its PR body say
they stay demoted "until `just refresh-chebi`".

**That instruction cannot be followed.** #199 established that the published
semsql artifact is byte-identical to the local one: both are release 252, while
kg-microbe is on 253. Running `refresh-chebi` deletes ~4.7 GB, re-downloads
~760 MB, and lands back on 252. The lag is upstream of MIM, in the semsql build
pipeline, and no action in this repo clears it.

So the 6 are blocked on an **external event** — the bbop-sqlite build catching up
to ChEBI 253 — not on a task. They should not sit in the backlog as though
someone can pick them up.

## What to do

- [ ] Correct the six manifest rows and the surrounding note to say the block is
      upstream, so the next curator does not spend an hour proving it. (Doing
      this on #205's branch before merge.)
- [ ] Leave them `UNMAPPED`. They are unverifiable *here* until the build moves;
      `PENDING_REVIEW` would invite a review that cannot be completed.
- [ ] Re-check with `just check-chebi-currency`. When it reports the published
      artifact differs, refresh, confirm the six resolve, and restore them the
      same way #205 restored the 11 — same `RESTORED_AFTER_FALSE_POSITIVE` event
      shape.

Blocked-on-upstream; not actionable in MIM today. Related: #197, #198, #206.

comments.body:
Re-verified on `main` @ `703368ac` (2026-08-07), during the review of PR #302. **Five of the six are no longer blocked; one still is.** Re-scoping rather than closing.

## Five were resolved by re-grounding, not by a refresh

The issue's framing — "blocked on the semsql build, not on a refresh anyone can run" — was correct, and the microbedecoder residual work took the other exit: ground to a term the local build *can* validate. All five resolve with canonical label match, no deprecation:

- carbomycin → `NCIT:C166659` · colistin sulfate → `NCIT:C386` · lysostaphin → `NCIT:C166895` · polymyxin B → `NCIT:C61894` (all EXACT_MATCH against `ncit.db`)
- netilmicin → `CHEBI:7528` *netilmycin* (`chebi.db`); the duplicate record was merged in, so the surviving file is `Netilmycin.yaml`

None of the five carries an intent to move back. Published SSSOM and `docs/data/` agree, with zero occurrences of the dead accessions.

## Gentamicin is still blocked, and says so itself

`data/ingredients/mapped/Gentamicin.yaml` holds `CHEBI:17833` *gentamycin* as a deliberate stand-in. Its own `CORRECTED` history entry (curator `issue_213_premise_correction`):

> `CHEBI:759884` is live and labelled "gentamicin", verified against OLS4. It is absent from the local semsql build only (#197/#207/#210). The `CHEBI:17833` gentamycin grounding stands as the term this repo can validate, and is the same aminoglycoside, but **`CHEBI:759884` is the exact term and this record should move back to it once the build carries it**.

The blocking condition is unchanged: local build **252**, kg-microbe **253**, and `check-chebi-currency` reports the published semsql artifact byte-identical to the local one — so `just refresh-chebi` still cannot deliver it.

**Proposed re-scope:** this issue now tracks one record. Close it when `CHEBI:759884` resolves locally and `Gentamicin.yaml` is re-grounded via `reground_mapped_record.py` (#267), or when a curator rules that `CHEBI:17833` should stand permanently — which is a legitimate answer, and would close this outright.

## A question the re-grounding raises, which nobody has ruled on

All six accessions **do** exist in kg-microbe's own ChEBI 253:

```
$ gzcat ../kg-microbe/data/raw/chebi.owl.gz | grep -oE "CHEBI_(753395|756054|748901|759883|759086|759884)" | sort | uniq -c
  46 CHEBI_748901    3 CHEBI_753395    6 CHEBI_756054
  57 CHEBI_759086   26 CHEBI_759883   59 CHEBI_759884
```

So for the four NCIT re-groundings, MIM publishes an NCIT term while the downstream consumer already carries the exact CHEBI one. That is a **sourcing divergence, not an error** — NCIT:C166895 *Lysostaphin* is a correct grounding — but it means MIM's ontology choice was driven by a local build limitation rather than by curation policy, and the limitation is invisible to consumers. Worth a deliberate ruling once the build catches up rather than letting it stand by default.

Related: #249 (closed — none of the six ids is a record identifier any more), #197, #205, #213, #210 / PR #302.

**Ruled by the curator (2026-08-07): NCIT is correct.** Closing.

These five are **final groundings, not stopgaps** waiting on a build refresh. A term MIM can resolve and label-check is the better published mapping, and that judgement does not expire when the local semsql build catches up to ChEBI.

| record | grounding | displaced |
|---|---|---|
| `Carbomycin` | `NCIT:C166659` | `CHEBI:756054` |
| `Colistin_Sulfate` | `NCIT:C386` | `CHEBI:759883` |
| `Lysostaphin` | `NCIT:C166895` | `CHEBI:753395` |
| `Polymyxin_B` | `NCIT:C61894` | `CHEBI:759086` |
| `Gentamicin` | `CHEBI:17833` | `CHEBI:759884` |

**Gentamicin's deferred intent is superseded.** The `issue_213_premise_correction` entry said the record "should move back to [`CHEBI:759884`] once the build carries it". It should not. `CHEBI:17833` *gentamycin* resolves, so MIM's ordinary source preference (`curie.py::PREFIX_RANK`, CHEBI above NCIT) already selects it. The four NCIT groundings are that same preference order working — CHEBI simply had nothing validatable to offer — not an exception to it.

## Why this needed recording, not just deciding

All five displaced accessions **do** exist in kg-microbe's own ChEBI 253. Left as-is, a future sync against the consumer's ontology would have read as an invitation to "restore" them — especially with two records stating the displaced id was "the exact term". So each of the five now carries a `CURATOR_RULING` event ending:

> Do not re-ground to `CHEBI:NNNNNN` without a new curator decision.

Applied by `scripts/apply_ncit_grounding_ruling.py` — idempotent, schema-validated on write, and it **refuses** if a record has moved off the grounding being ruled on rather than stapling a decision onto a mapping nobody ruled on. Written to `data/curated/` (source of truth) and projected via `export-individual`; editing the per-record files directly is the #148 trap.

## Generalised

The rule is written up under **Ontology Selection Guide** in `.claude/skills/map-media-ingredients/SKILL.md`, so it applies to the next case rather than only these five:

> **A term you cannot resolve is not a candidate.** The priority order ranks ontologies you can *check*. When the exact CHEBI term exists upstream but is absent locally, ground to a resolvable term in the next ontology that has one and treat that as final. NCIT is the usual answer for antibiotics and drug substances.

## Gates

`validate-all` 2848 files / **0 errors, 0 warnings** · `qc-roundtrip` · `qc-duplicate-ids` (baseline unchanged) · `qc-sssom` Rules A/B1/B2/B3 · `check-instruction-refs` · `qc-flat-coverage`.

That last one earned its keep: it caught `docs/data/ingredients.json` going stale, because `curation_history` feeds its `last_curated`/`curator` fields. Confirmed it was fresh immediately before the change, regenerated with `export-browser`, re-verified. The SSSOM is untouched — no mapping changed, only the record of the decision.

The upstream lag itself is unchanged and still real (build **252** vs ChEBI **253**, refresh is a no-op because the published semsql artifact is byte-identical). It is simply no longer blocking anything here.

Shipped in PR #302 (`d5e90353`). Related: #249 (closed), #197, #205, #213, #210.

title: Gentamicin is grounded to a stand-in term because CHEBI:759884 is missing from the local semsql build
